title: The Girl with the Warm Heart

pages.text: The Girl with the Warm Heart
Gerda and Kai were best friends. They lived next door to each other, high up under the roofs. Between their windows grew a box of red roses, and they played there every day.
One snowy night, Grandma told them a story. "The Snow Queen flies with the snowflakes," she said. "Wherever she looks, the windows freeze." Kai laughed. "I'm not scared of her!"
Far away, a naughty troll broke a magic mirror. A tiny splinter flew into Kai's eye, and another into his heart. Ouch! Now everything looked ugly to Kai. "Roses are silly," he said.
Kai went sledding in the town square. A big white sleigh came by, and Kai tied his little sled to it. Whoosh! The sleigh flew up into the snowy sky. It was the Snow Queen!
The Snow Queen kissed Kai on the forehead. Now he did not feel cold at all. He forgot Gerda. He forgot Grandma. He forgot his home. Away they flew, to the far, far north.
Gerda waited and waited. When spring came, she put on her new red shoes. "I will find Kai," she said. She climbed into a little boat, and the river carried her away.
The boat stopped by a garden full of flowers. A kind old lady gave Gerda cherries and brushed her hair, and Gerda forgot about Kai. Then she saw a red rose. "Kai!" she cried, and she ran on.
A clever raven hopped up to Gerda. "Caw! A boy lives in the palace," he said. But the boy was a prince, not Kai. The prince and princess were kind. They gave Gerda warm boots and a golden coach.
In the dark forest, robbers stopped the coach! A wild little robber girl shouted, "She's mine!" She took Gerda home to sleep with her pigeons and her big reindeer.
At night, the pigeons cooed, "We saw Kai! He went north with the Snow Queen." The robber girl was wild, but she was kind too. She set the reindeer free. "Take Gerda to the Snow Queen!"
The reindeer ran and ran, over the snow, under the dancing lights of the north. Gerda held on tight. It got colder, and colder, and colder.
At last, they came to the palace of ice. Angry snowflakes flew at Gerda to stop her. But Gerda was not afraid. She blew warm breaths, puff, puff, and the snowflakes melted away.

Inside, Kai sat alone on a frozen lake, blue with cold. Gerda ran and hugged him tight. Her warm tears fell on his heart, and the ice melted. Kai cried too, and the splinter washed out of his eye. "Gerda!"
Together, they went home. Spring came with them, and the red roses bloomed again. Gerda's warm heart had melted the ice. A kind, warm heart is stronger than any ice. And yours is too. The end.
